title: EATF Action Evidence Package toolkit
description: Open toolkit for creating, inspecting, and offline-verifying Action Evidence Packages (.aep): a hybrid RSA-4096 plus ML-DSA-65 signer, two verifiers (TypeScript and Python), both built by Tyche Institute, sign/verify/inspect CLIs, RFC 9881 public-key encoding, JSON schemas, positive and negative conformance vectors, and a deterministic offline downgrade lab.
notes: Version 0.7.3 makes the Python verifier compare the CMS message-digest attribute of an RFC 3161 time-stamp token with the encapsulated TSTInfo (RFC 5652 section 5.4). In v0.7.2 and earlier Python verified the TSA signature over the signed attributes but not that those attributes cover the TSTInfo, so a genuine token whose genTime or message imprint had been edited after signing, including a token taken from another package with its imprint rewritten to match, still verified; the TypeScript verifier (TypeScript and Python are both built by Tyche Institute) already rejected both with TSA_SIGNATURE_INVALID, and Python now does too. Python also reports an imprint under a hash other than SHA-256 as TSA_IMPRINT_UNVERIFIABLE, as TypeScript does. docs/authority-record-v1-scope.md and scripts/authority-record-crosscheck.py explain and reproduce why the root verifiers reject every verify=true package of the frozen authority-record corpus under artifacts/authority-record-v1/: its time-stamp tokens are certificate-less placeholders that bind none of its packages, and the root verifiers do not implement that profile's warrant, accepting-authority and mandate checks; the frozen artifact is unchanged. The 5 accepted and 8 rejected conformance vectors, the 42 lab observations and the 21 decision-path cases give the same results as in v0.7.2. Previous version v0.7.2 is doi:10.5281/zenodo.23466228 under concept doi:10.5281/zenodo.21763055; releases through v0.5.0 remain under earlier concept doi:10.5281/zenodo.21511608.
